subject.title: Feature request: config option to suppress transient tool error warnings

question: Should OpenClaw add a new normal-chat tool-error delivery policy such as `messages.toolErrorDelivery: all | final | off`, or keep the existing boolean `messages.suppressToolErrors` plus safety fallback?
rationale: The remaining work adds public config and changes when users are warned about failed mutating tools after a successful-looking assistant reply; source and related PRs show partial fixes, but not a maintainer-approved delivery policy.

options.title: Add an explicit delivery policy
options.body: Introduce a documented enum/default that keeps current behavior by default while allowing hosted/team-chat deployments to opt into final-only or off behavior with focused upgrade tests.

options.title: Keep the boolean only
options.body: Treat `messages.suppressToolErrors` as the supported all-off operator escape hatch and close or narrow this issue to docs around the existing behavior.

options.title: Defer to channel-specific policy
options.body: Avoid a global config until Telegram, Discord, Feishu, and gateway lifecycle warning semantics are designed together.

recommendation.title: Add an explicit delivery policy
recommendation.body: Introduce a documented enum/default that keeps current behavior by default while allowing hosted/team-chat deployments to opt into final-only or off behavior with focused upgrade tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged partial fix and explicitly scoped this issue as the remaining broader delivery-policy/config work.
